body:
| | | |
---
| | |
# 2023 September e-newsletter
News and information for District 5 in San Mateo County.
---
|
---
|
---
| **Bold action required to combat organized retail theft**
---
| Nationwide, we see on the news every night how organized criminal groups are able to ransack businesses and avoid going to jail as individuals only face misdemeanor charges if they have stolen less than $950 in merchandise.
Some of you may have seen a press conference I conducted that was widely covered by the local media and even the national press.
I said ‘enough is enough’ and that whatever the state of California is currently doing is simply not working.

We’ve seen these crimes committed locally at Hillsdale, Tanforan and Serramonte shopping centers, our Ross stores, Sephora and even Lego stores.

To combat the epidemic of organized retail theft locally I am calling on a San Mateo Countywide task force amongst law enforcement and the business community to be formed to tackle this issue head on.

I imagine the taskforce to be similar to the Vehicle Theft Task Force the county has now and have heard a deep interest in law enforcement in establishing a similar task force related to retail theft.

I will be issuing a letter to the Sheriff’s Office and county Police Chiefs Association soon to commence this process
---
and will be asking our county executive’s office and chambers of commerce to also participate in the taskforce. I also sent a letter to our local state elected officials following the press conference demanding the state Legislature take action to combat the epidemic. With that, I’m proud to announce that Gov. Gavin Newsom pledged the largest-ever single investment to combat organized retail crime — **$267,118,293, his office announced Tuesday, Sept. 12 **As part of a competitive grant process, he is recommending the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) award funding to 55 local law enforcement agencies across California. If approved by the Board, the funding, part of the Governor’s [Real Public Safety Plan](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=5ad5ee5fce&e=c0babbc643), is slated to be dispersed on October 1, 2023, to police departments, sheriffs’ departments and district attorney offices in every region of the state to prevent and investigate cases of organized retail theft and arrest and prosecute more suspects, according to Newsom’s office. This is a step in the right direction and I will continue to work locally to protect the public for organized crime rings.
---
| ******County program creates 32 new home cook businesses** Did you know that California became the first state to legalize sales of home-cooked meals with laws passed in 2018 and 2019 for “Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operations” or MEHKO?

I am proud to say that while serving on the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors I sponsored a resolution in 2019 affirming the county’s support for MEHKO and then sponsored an ordinance that allowed for a 2-year pilot in 2021, one of the first in the state to allow home cooks to come out of the shadows.

Now, I am proud to announce that MEHKO has created 32 new businesses and has become a permanent reality in San Mateo County with action the Board took at its Sept. 12 meeting.

Let me tell you a story about Mary. And there are a lot of Marys out there. Mary had to close her housecleaning business of 2 decades or more because the work became too backbreaking for her.

She lost tens of thousands a year in wages and could no longer contribute to the family’s income like she could before. She was looking for a new path and wanted to work but because of certain disabilities she was just unable to.

But Mary is one incredible cook I can tell you who has always hosted big dinners for family and friends with super healthy food. But before MEHKO, if Mary wanted to sell any of her delicious meals, she would have been literally breaking the law.

In 2021, she heard about San Mateo County’s MEHKO pilot, applied for the program, took all the tests and certifications required by the state and county and passed them all.

Now she is the proud owner of Mary’s Small Kitchen in San Mateo. She can work on her time, decide her own menus and even serve people in her home hot home-cooked delicious meals such as meat loaf, lasagnas and her famous grilled chicken sandwiches.

Her home is routinely inspected by Environmental Health to ensure the food she prepares is just as safe as it would be at any restaurant.
If you look at the roster of home cooks you see they are spread throughout the county from Brisbane and Menlo Park, San Mateo, Daly City and more.

You also see that 84 percent of these businesses are owned by women, which shows the need and importance of MEHKO. This is about the Marys of the world. Uplifting those in need and helping them succeed when they otherwise thought they couldn’t.

Congratulations to all the home cooks out there who have created small businesses and for feeding our communities and thanks to Supervisor Ray Mueller for cosponsoring the ordinance with me.

To learn more and how to apply go to: [https://www.smchealth.org/node/4020](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=fa57ccaa0d&e=c0babbc643).
---
---
| **County creates guaranteed basic income program for foster youth** In a unanimous vote, the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to provide current and former foster youth ages 18 up to 22 with $1,000 a month in the county’s first guaranteed income program. I was proud to sponsor the resolution with Supervisor Noelia Corzo.

About 70 eligible young adults will receive a direct deposit for up to 18 months.
Our goal is to disrupt the cycle of poverty.

Foster youth face so many challenges that most of us cannot imagine. We as a community want to help these young adults finish high school and go on to college or trades programs without so much of the crushing burden of making ends meet in a county with such a high cost of living.

Foster youth remain very vulnerable to housing instability and homelessness as they age-out of the system. Concrete economic support allows for some relief from the economic pressures that might otherwise push them out of San Mateo County and away from their support systems and friends.

Recipients can use the monthly stipend as they see fit, for education, transportation, housing, food and other needs.

With a secure monthly income floor, it is anticipated that participants will be better able to take advantage of services provided to transitional age foster youth. These include access to educational and financial counselors and a range of support staff that will provide linkages to health and mental health services, employment services and enrichment activities.

The encouragement and financial support are needed to help current and former foster youth navigate the complexities of lease agreements, school and work applications and other responsibilities without families to guide them.

The first $1,000 direct deposits are expected to begin around the New Year. Supervisors approved the program as a pilot that includes a thorough evaluation that will test the impact.
---
| **
This month launches a new Latino Heritage Month speaker series** The inaugural Latino Heritage Month Speaker Series kicks off on Friday, Sept. 15 with Civil Rights activist and Medal of Freedom recipient Sylvia Mendez at the San Mateo Performing Arts Center.

Mendez is also a retired nurse who at age eight, played an instrumental role in the Mendez v. Westminster case, the landmark desegregation case of 1946. The case successfully ended de jure segregation in California and paved the way for integration and the American civil rights movement.

Organized by the Latino Leaders Coalition of the Bay Area (LLCBA), the speaker series celebrates and showcases the rich diversity of the Latino community and is focused on reaching students to help them turn their dreams into reality.

LLCBA is a newly formed organization of San Mateo County Latino school board members and superintendents, which was established to educate, engage, and empower Latino students, families and educators throughout San Mateo County. Kudos to Jennifer Blanco, a San Bruno Park School District trustee and founding member of the coalition, for her effort in launching this exciting new speaker series.
---
| **
Geese get a reprieve in Foster City** It’s been a bit more than a year now since I first conducted a rally with animal rights activists on Aug. 26, 2022 to protest Foster City’s decision to kill 100 geese at the cost of $100,000 to manage the poop problem the birds create.

I was joined by advocates including Erik Allen with Direct Action Everywhere and local elected officials including Foster City Councilman Patrick Sullivan at the rally to urge city leaders to find more humane ways to address the poop problem including developing a comprehensive plan that includes strategic natural landscaping, artificial turf and adding buffer zones along the banks of the city’s lagoons.

I’m proud to say a year later, the city has decided to develop a management plan that will include only non-lethal strategies to manage the geese who call Foster City home.

I said at the rally that we need to learn to live with the geese because, after all, “Everybody Poops.” Marin County nonprofit In Defense of Animals announced that it is giving its “Happy Honk” award to Foster City officials for deciding to use nonlethal means to manage the Canada geese population in the area.

Kudos to the advocates and leaders in Foster City including Mayor Jon Froomin and the City Council for working tirelessly to save the geese from death.

**Battling food insecurity **
Food insecurity is a problem some residents may still face as we continue to emerge from the pandemic. Here are some resources residents can access: **CalFresh:**
Is a program for people with low-income who meet federal income eligibility rules and want to add to their budget to put healthy and nutritious food on the table. Website: [https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-nutrition/calfresh](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=464e78226d&e=c0babbc643) Contact: (650) 802-6576, [antorres@smcgov.org](mailto:antorres@smcgov.org) **Daly City Partnership:**
DC Partnership is a local partnership that was formed to guide collaborative efforts and connect our community to services that promote well-being. Check out their website for times and locations. clean_body: | | | | | | | 2023 September e-newsletter News and information for District 5 in San Mateo County. | | | Bold action required to combat organized retail theft | Nationwide, we see on the news every night how organized criminal groups are able to ransack businesses and avoid going to jail as individuals only face misdemeanor charges if they have stolen less than $950 in merchandise. Some of you may have seen a press conference I conducted that was widely covered by the local media and even the national press. I said ‘enough is enough’ and that whatever the state of California is currently doing is simply not working. We’ve seen these crimes committed locally at Hillsdale, Tanforan and Serramonte shopping centers, our Ross stores, Sephora and even Lego stores. To combat the epidemic of organized retail theft locally I am calling on a San Mateo Countywide task force amongst law enforcement and the business community to be formed to tackle this issue head on. I imagine the taskforce to be similar to the Vehicle Theft Task Force the county has now and have heard a deep interest in law enforcement in establishing a similar task force related to retail theft. I will be issuing a letter to the Sheriff’s Office and county Police Chiefs Association soon to commence this process and will be asking our county executive’s office and chambers of commerce to also participate in the taskforce. I also sent a letter to our local state elected officials following the press conference demanding the state Legislature take action to combat the epidemic. With that, I’m proud to announce that Gov. Gavin Newsom pledged the largest-ever single investment to combat organized retail crime — $267,118,293, his office announced Tuesday, Sept. 12 As part of a competitive grant process, he is recommending the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) award funding to 55 local law enforcement agencies across California. If approved by the Board, the funding, part of the Governor’s , is slated to be dispersed on October 1, 2023, to police departments, sheriffs’ departments and district attorney offices in every region of the state to prevent and investigate cases of organized retail theft and arrest and prosecute more suspects, according to Newsom’s office. This is a step in the right direction and I will continue to work locally to protect the public for organized crime rings. | ****County program creates 32 new home cook businesses Did you know that California became the first state to legalize sales of home-cooked meals with laws passed in 2018 and 2019 for “Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operations” or MEHKO? I am proud to say that while serving on the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors I sponsored a resolution in 2019 affirming the county’s support for MEHKO and then sponsored an ordinance that allowed for a 2-year pilot in 2021, one of the first in the state to allow home cooks to come out of the shadows. Now, I am proud to announce that MEHKO has created 32 new businesses and has become a permanent reality in San Mateo County with action the Board took at its Sept. 12 meeting. Let me tell you a story about Mary. And there are a lot of Marys out there. Mary had to close her housecleaning business of 2 decades or more because the work became too backbreaking for her. She lost tens of thousands a year in wages and could no longer contribute to the family’s income like she could before. She was looking for a new path and wanted to work but because of certain disabilities she was just unable to. But Mary is one incredible cook I can tell you who has always hosted big dinners for family and friends with super healthy food. But before MEHKO, if Mary wanted to sell any of her delicious meals, she would have been literally breaking the law. In 2021, she heard about San Mateo County’s MEHKO pilot, applied for the program, took all the tests and certifications required by the state and county and passed them all. Now she is the proud owner of Mary’s Small Kitchen in San Mateo. She can work on her time, decide her own menus and even serve people in her home hot home-cooked delicious meals such as meat loaf, lasagnas and her famous grilled chicken sandwiches. Her home is routinely inspected by Environmental Health to ensure the food she prepares is just as safe as it would be at any restaurant. If you look at the roster of home cooks you see they are spread throughout the county from Brisbane and Menlo Park, San Mateo, Daly City and more. You also see that 84 percent of these businesses are owned by women, which shows the need and importance of MEHKO. This is about the Marys of the world. Uplifting those in need and helping them succeed when they otherwise thought they couldn’t. Congratulations to all the home cooks out there who have created small businesses and for feeding our communities and thanks to Supervisor Ray Mueller for cosponsoring the ordinance with me. To learn more and how to apply go to: . | County creates guaranteed basic income program for foster youth In a unanimous vote, the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to provide current and former foster youth ages 18 up to 22 with $1,000 a month in the county’s first guaranteed income program. I was proud to sponsor the resolution with Supervisor Noelia Corzo. About 70 eligible young adults will receive a direct deposit for up to 18 months. Our goal is to disrupt the cycle of poverty. Foster youth face so many challenges that most of us cannot imagine. We as a community want to help these young adults finish high school and go on to college or trades programs without so much of the crushing burden of making ends meet in a county with such a high cost of living. Foster youth remain very vulnerable to housing instability and homelessness as they age-out of the system. Concrete economic support allows for some relief from the economic pressures that might otherwise push them out of San Mateo County and away from their support systems and friends. Recipients can use the monthly stipend as they see fit, for education, transportation, housing, food and other needs. With a secure monthly income floor, it is anticipated that participants will be better able to take advantage of services provided to transitional age foster youth. These include access to educational and financial counselors and a range of support staff that will provide linkages to health and mental health services, employment services and enrichment activities. The encouragement and financial support are needed to help current and former foster youth navigate the complexities of lease agreements, school and work applications and other responsibilities without families to guide them. The first $1,000 direct deposits are expected to begin around the New Year. Supervisors approved the program as a pilot that includes a thorough evaluation that will test the impact. | This month launches a new Latino Heritage Month speaker series The inaugural Latino Heritage Month Speaker Series kicks off on Friday, Sept. 15 with Civil Rights activist and Medal of Freedom recipient Sylvia Mendez at the San Mateo Performing Arts Center. Mendez is also a retired nurse who at age eight, played an instrumental role in the Mendez v. Westminster case, the landmark desegregation case of 1946. The case successfully ended de jure segregation in California and paved the way for integration and the American civil rights movement. Organized by the Latino Leaders Coalition of the Bay Area (LLCBA), the speaker series celebrates and showcases the rich diversity of the Latino community and is focused on reaching students to help them turn their dreams into reality. LLCBA is a newly formed organization of San Mateo County Latino school board members and superintendents, which was established to educate, engage, and empower Latino students, families and educators throughout San Mateo County. Kudos to Jennifer Blanco, a San Bruno Park School District trustee and founding member of the coalition, for her effort in launching this exciting new speaker series. | Geese get a reprieve in Foster City It’s been a bit more than a year now since I first conducted a rally with animal rights activists on Aug. 26, 2022 to protest Foster City’s decision to kill 100 geese at the cost of $100,000 to manage the poop problem the birds create. I was joined by advocates including Erik Allen with Direct Action Everywhere and local elected officials including Foster City Councilman Patrick Sullivan at the rally to urge city leaders to find more humane ways to address the poop problem including developing a comprehensive plan that includes strategic natural landscaping, artificial turf and adding buffer zones along the banks of the city’s lagoons. I’m proud to say a year later, the city has decided to develop a management plan that will include only non-lethal strategies to manage the geese who call Foster City home. I said at the rally that we need to learn to live with the geese because, after all, “Everybody Poops.” Marin County nonprofit In Defense of Animals announced that it is giving its “Happy Honk” award to Foster City officials for deciding to use nonlethal means to manage the Canada geese population in the area. Kudos to the advocates and leaders in Foster City including Mayor Jon Froomin and the City Council for working tirelessly to save the geese from death. Battling food insecurity Food insecurity is a problem some residents may still face as we continue to emerge from the pandemic. Here are some resources residents can access: CalFresh: Is a program for people with low-income who meet federal income eligibility rules and want to add to their budget to put healthy and nutritious food on the table. Website: Contact: (650) 802-6576, mailto:antorres@smcgov.org Daly City Partnership: DC Partnership is a local partnership that was formed to guide collaborative efforts and connect our community to services that promote well-being. Sen. Tommy Tuberville’s blockade of military appointments continues to leave our military in a vulnerable position. According to America’s military leaders, his actions are actively aiding our adversaries. It is unimaginable to me that an individual has put their political gimmicks over the interests of our entire country. Because of his actions, the Pentagon and our nation's service secretaries have been forced to spend their valuable time advocating for Tuberville to end his blockade. This move takes away the Pentagon’s valuable time and energy — when it should be focused on addressing threats to our national security.

I will continue to pressure Sen. Tuberville to end his dangerous blockade. As a former CIA officer, I know how important every facet of our national security apparatus is. I won’t stand for this disregard for our servicemembers.

I have one priority: serving the people of Virginia. I will never let politics get in the way of my oath to serve. **I’ll be honest with you, Peter:** Over the years, in Ohio, we've seen manufacturing jobs shipped overseas because of bad trade deals, prices skyrocketing as wages failed to keep up, and hopes for a comfortable retirement dashed. That's why I've devoted my life to fighting for the Dignity of Work – the idea that hard work should pay off for everyone, no matter who you are, where you live, or what kind of work you do.
**Every day in the Senate, I’m fighting for _you_. Right now, Mitch McConnell and the GOP need to flip only two seats to retake Senate control – and experts at _Politico_ say it could all come down to Ohio. Last year’s Senate race here was one of the most costly in the nation, and _NBC News_ reports this one could be “even nastier and more expensive.”

**That's why I simply cannot win this race – and Democrats simply cannot hold on to our narrow Senate majority – without grassroots support from folks like you. As one of the most vulnerable senators in the country, I'm personally asking:**
[**Will you please split $5 between my campaign and Patty Murray's to help us hit our midnight fundraising goal, power my reelection campaign to victory, and keep the Senate blue?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/69694889/426965818/348274074?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&amount=5&refcode=jtk124-bu-nd&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNTA2MzNhYy04MzUyLWVlMTEtOTkzNy0wMDIyNDgzMmU4MTEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hFAPQGtLy6oKxsQjATHsjYDVfkbmbgQZvaVBDmvwpI8=)
This is gonna be a heck of a fight, but with you by my side, I know we can beat the odds and continue making much-needed progress for workers and families. Thanks for being on our team.
With gratitude,

Sherrod

We’re less than six months to Election Day, and I have two important updates:
1. Last week the LA Times released a poll that showed us **three points behind** our opponent. That same poll found **36% of voters are still undecided** , so reaching those undecided Californians will be the key to pulling ahead and winning this race.

2. Our federal end of quarter fundraising deadline is**September 30th**. We’ll have to report how much we’ve raised over the past three months, and because we’ve been outraised the past two quarters, it’s critical we pull ahead.

body:
#
Yesterday, Speaker Kevin McCarthy announced his support for an impeachment inquiry into President Biden. This comes at the same time that House Republicans are threatening to oust McCarthy unless he shutdowns the government on September 30.
Republicans know that the chaos makes it impossible to govern. And for many of them, **that’s exactly the goal.**
[The ‘far left’ and the ‘far right’ are often compared, but the reality is that while MAGA Republicans sow chaos for the sake of chaos, Alexandria is fighting for universal healthcare, a $15 minimum wage and other just policies. Will you make a $5 contribution today so that she can continue her campaign for progress?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20230913.ZG_hYb&refcode=em20230913-4977-P_FND_EGR_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=4977%2E2526796%2Eyxzbyq)

Republicans have shown, time and again, that they have no respect for our democratic institutions. They want government to fail.
**Every government shutdown in the last 30 years occurred when Republicans had control of the House of Representatives.** Last time it happened, it drove people to food pantries and forced an $8 billion hit to the economy. They treat people missing paychecks like it’s no big deal.
Alexandria came to Congress to fight for working families like hers, and she will continue to call out Republicans' chaos and disarray. [Will you make a $5 contribution right now to power our fight?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20230913.ZG_hYb&refcode=em20230913-4977-P_FND_EGR_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=4977%2E2526796%2Eyxzbyq)

In solidarity,
Team AOC

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: I’m here today courtesy of three bags of M&Ms and a very cooperative toddler.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
I’m sure a lot of you know this story. Washing dishes, bathing children, doing laundry at 11:00 at night...

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=59%2E4032634%2EF_tN3s)
---
Years ago, I was a new mom at home with my baby Amelia, and I got this grand idea that I could go to law school. I headed off to a state law school that cost $450 a semester, but first...I needed to find child care. I thought, _“How hard could that be?”_ Well, I found out just how hard. I spent weeks visiting all kinds of places, and none of them were right. Either the kids looked miserable, the place had a funny smell, the waiting list was a mile long, the cost was way outside our budget... It was getting down to the last week before law school classes were going to start, and I was starting to sweat. But then I found a truly great place. It had a cheerful teacher, a nice play area, nothing smelled funny...but there was one problem: They only took children who were “dependably” potty trained. At the time, Amelia was not quite _dependable_ , but I couldn’t let that stop me. I had about five days to get my toddler **dependably** potty trained. I just want you to know that I’m here today courtesy of three bags of M&Ms, and a very cooperative toddler. But here’s the thing: Child care never stopped being an issue for me — just like for so many working parents today. It was this weight I had to carry around every single day and it never let up. Eventually I graduated from law school pregnant with baby number two, Alex, and then I got a teaching job at a law school in Houston and I was beyond excited. I loved teaching and I knew that this job was what I was meant to do, so I did whatever it took to make it work while also caring for my family. I still got dinner on the table every night — even if most nights it was late and the kids were cranky. We ate a lot of stuff from boxes that said _“Just add water!”_ I’m sure a lot of you know this story. Washing dishes, bathing children, doing laundry at 11:00 at night, and then starting to prepare for the next day — falling into bed sometime in the early hours of the morning. It was hard — but I could do hard. It was exhausting — but I could handle exhausting. But the thing that eventually sank me? Child care. In the space of a few months, I tried everything to find help. A babysitter, a daycare center, another daycare center, a neighbor. One day I picked up my son Alex from a daycare, and he had been left in a soggy diaper for heaven only knows how long. I was upset with the daycare people, but more than anything else, I was upset with myself. I felt like I was failing my baby. So one night after I put both kids to bed, my 78-year-old Aunt Bee called long distance from Oklahoma just to see how I was doing. I said _“fiiiine”_ in a thin voice. And then I just started to cry. I couldn’t hold it together any longer. I told my Aunt Bee that I was going to quit my job. I hadn’t thought about it much, but it just all started to crash down and the words just fell out of my mouth. I cried, I sobbed...I loved that job. But that was it. Finally I blew my nose, I got a drink of water, and then Aunt Bee said 11 words that changed my life forever: “I can’t get there tomorrow, but I can come on Thursday.” Two days later, she arrived at the airport with seven suitcases and a Pekingese named Buddy and she stayed for 16 years. | [](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/457?t=8&akid=59%2E4032634%2EF_tN3s)
---
Here’s the thing about this story: Without child care, I was a goner. Today I am a United States senator in part because my Aunt Bee rescued me on a Thursday about a zillion years ago.
I’m so, so grateful for my Aunt Bee, but so many families don’t have an emergency Aunt Bee solution. We live in the richest country in the history of the planet — and yet the child care crisis has just gotten worse and worse and worse since this story.
And if you can believe it, it’s about to get _even worse_ unless Congress votes to extend emergency funding at the end of this month. And MAGA Republicans are doing everything they can to cut off this funding.
Without this funding, at least 3.2 million children would lose their child care. 70,000 child care programs could shut their doors. Nearly a quarter of a million child care workers could lose their jobs.
I’m fighting like hell to get this emergency funding passed as a short-term solution, and to pass my Child Care for Every Community Act in the long-term. Under my plan, half of all American families would pay no more than $10 a day for child care, costs would be capped for everyone, no one would pay more than 7% of their income, and child care workers would get badly needed, well-deserved raises.
**[This issue is a part of my heart forever. And if it’s a part of yours, too, I want to hear from you. Please share with me how access to child care — or lack thereof — has impacted your life. Your story is very important to me.](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/wfs-share-your-child-care-story/?source=EMZ16Q_CHD_E_20230913_V1S1_F&t=9&akid=59%2E4032634%2EF_tN3s)**
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

| | | Peter, For the 1.5 million people of Philadelphia, whether or not they live in safe, affordable communities with good jobs over the next few years will be largely decided by who they have representing them on the City Council. In every City Council election since 1951, Democrats have won five of the seven at-large council seats, which is the most any single party can hold. The last two seats are reserved for a minority party. **In practice, this has meant that two Republicans automatically get a seat on the council to push their agenda to give major corporations and wealthy donors a break at the expense of services that working families rely on.** That is until Kendra Brooks beat every Republican on the ballot and became the first Working Families Party member of the City Council in 2019. Now, she’s running for re-election, and she and PAWFP Organizing Director Nicolas O’Rourke are coming to take both minority party seats and kick Republicans OUT. The election is less than two months away, and we need your help to reach Philadelphians about what’s at stake in this election and why they should vote on the WFP line. **[If you know anybody in Philadelphia (really, anybody!), you can make a major impact by joining a virtual postcard party tomorrow, Thursday September 14 at 6 PM ET. The GOP and conservative special interest groups have been playing a 50-year chess game to elect far-right extremists to every level of government to manipulate our country and attack our rights and freedoms. But badass young people have a habit of being underestimated, from March For Our Lives to the Sunrise Movement to the Movement for Black Lives. And when we demonstrate our collective power, we scare the shit out of Republicans.

body:
Presidential Candidate Vivek Ramaswamy will be our KEYNOTE Speaker at Mackinac on Friday, September 22nd. | | |
---
| |
---
| |
# Party of the Constitution
---
**VIVEK RAMASWAMY,** Presidential Candidate, Business Leader, and Author, has confirmed his attendance and will be the KEYNOTE Speaker at the Mackinac Leadership Conference on Friday, September 22nd.
The **NEW MIGOP** , which is led by **Constitutionalists** , is committed to making this conference the best one yet. We have an impressive lineup of speakers, including JIM CAVIEZEL, KARI LAKE, ZUBY, ALEX NEWMAN, and now Presidential Candidate VIVEK RAMASWAMY. We are confident that the upcoming Mackinac Republican Leadership Conference will be a truly memorable experience.
Vivek is an American business leader and New York Times bestselling author of Woke, Inc.: Inside Corporate America’s Social Justice Scam, along with his second book, Nation of Victims: Identity Politics, the Death of Merit, and the Path Back to Excellence, and Capitalist Punishment: How Wall Street is Using Your Money to Create a Country You Didn’t Vote For.
Left-leaning media has called him one of the “intellectual godfathers of the anti-woke movement” (Politico) and the “right’s leading anti-ESG crusader” (Axios and Bloomberg). He was dubbed “The C.E.O. of Anti-Woke” by The New Yorker. These movements are now popularized in mainstream conservative thought.
Born and raised in Cincinnati, Ohio, he often recounts the sage advice from his father: “If you’re going to stand out, then you might as well be outstanding.” This set the course for his life: a nationally ranked tennis player and the valedictorian of his high school, St. Xavier. He went on to graduate summa cum laude in Biology from Harvard and received his J.D. from Yale Law School while working at a hedge fund. He then started a biotech company, Roivant Sciences, where he oversaw the development of five drugs that went on to become FDA-approved.
In 2022, he founded Strive, an Ohio-based asset management firm that directly competes with asset managers like BlackRock, State Street, Vanguard, and others, who use the money of everyday citizens to advance environmental and social agendas that many citizens and capital owners disagree with.
Vivek is married to Apoorva, a throat surgeon and Assistant Professor at the Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. They live in Columbus, Ohio, where they are raising their two sons.
For additional details about our Mackinac Island Conference, please [click here](https://migop.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0bcd38e28909007274d8cce33&id=1937a07c63&e=a2af77507c).

We cannot wait to see you at this historic conference.

| | | Did you see?

I joined Nicolle Wallace on MSNBC last week to discuss our new ad. Click here to watch Nicolle’s reactions to it and then please consider supporting us as we spread the word about the leading cause of death for kids in America:

| | [Watch Now](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/wehEm_vu1NBVXOKYSqOxTOi34aJoCJC1EivM7Ih953wQ3U5yR8LFp9N37s5CvN3bqt3C4Td3cWujO6Na4PoYpZ6qjGeOUrTEUw5s7_9CaV5HOVfNsS2DuEo6OPCOze_Uiz69cj4tCFu216dHo5YgDEnaquUblenB_bZ2G8YnqktD56fpyrzohHCQpP6OdZNP4aBRm-Ne06jlxMxuC4axrEWdUiTuJXkUrmfsNDUKtg5YRNLY2wWdpKSShya4xI7o9US0DfkK1WYME0hnNph8MhBtuuPCikcRhpVvYCYDqbuymalMBveehJnu9WS1fC4cfIo9WlU7SZGzegviaSjNfjLs4JrSa7qDAFLTlH7p60N1qCaPdby9BnrZoJSFNoEi/3zk/jHDgstuYRrG8XAir5ZQKvQ/h0/W9IAbdZOjubVEKiBftX0fFMD8KuU4ThS06MwP3VpgiU)
---

Nicolle is right, this new video is ominous and difficult to watch. But you know what is harder? Being 6 and learning about the active shooter plan on your first day of school, or getting a text from your kid that there is a shooter on campus.

This is the uncomfortable reality that we live in, but we don’t have to. As highlighted in my conversation on MSNBC, upwards of 80% of Americans support common sense gun laws like universal background checks and an assault weapons ban.

**It is weak politicians who are standing in the way of change. That’s why we made this ad.**

Peter, We all know by now that women running for office are facing an uphill battle. They’re subject to harassment online and even physical threats against themselves and their families. They’re faced with double standards and sexist questions. And they’re severely underfunded. Women raise only about 75% of their male counterparts, on average. That _matters._ Because in 90% of House races, **the candidate who spends more wins. ** Listen, we have a mid-month fundraising deadline coming up this week. body:
We need a government that puts parents first. |
---
| |
---
| |

| I want strong schools, Peter. But I also want strong families. Schools shouldn't be allowed to keep secrets about kids from their parents.

That's why I was happy to see the Orange Unified School District approve a policy _**requiring schools to notify parents if their children begin identifying as a different gender.**_

Parents know what's best for their kids. Schools need _more_ communication with parents, not _less._

I'm running for Congress to fight for a government that puts parents - not bureaucrats - first. _But I need to know if you're standing with me._
[**_Can you let me know if I can count on YOUR support in our fight for Parents' Rights?_**](https://maxforoc.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0d5d4fbfb4ace920581f6c90d&id=f8c2a83e3a&e=86e91e802d)

---
| I've spoken to countless parents about this issue. We don't just need legislative solutions. We need action up and down the chain, from school boards to Congress.

That's why I plan to go to Washington to help fix the federal government's broken approach to education. [**_But this fight will be much easier if I know Orange County conservatives are standing with me._**](https://maxforoc.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=0d5d4fbfb4ace920581f6c90d&id=c63b05bbc0&e=86e91e802d)

I'm confident we can save our country and our schools if we're standing together.

Max Ukropina

| I grew up in a twenty-four-by-thirty-six foot house.
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/67?t=1&akid=1156%2E35263%2ELLg4-h)
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/2155?c0=tbe-em-tester.Z0aSwr&refcode=AU_STB_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20230913_PM1_V1_S1&t=4&akid=1156%2E35263%2ELLg4-h) Can I explain something, Peter? I grew up in a twenty-four-by-thirty-six foot house. I lost three fingers on my left hand in a meat grinding accident when I was a kid. I am and always will be a farmer, like my folks and like my grandparents. In fact, I’m very proud to be the only U.S. Senator who manages a full-time job outside the Senate — **as a farmer.** Every spring, I spend a lot of weeks working the stubble, getting equipment ready for planting, and out in the field seeding. Come summer, I am out there harvesting. I maintain my own heavy equipment and deliver my grain in a truck that’s a bit bigger than what any of my colleagues drive. I buy grease by the case and seeds by the ton. I butcher my own beef. My wife, Sharla, and I work the farm hand-in-hand. The task of scheduling my work in the Senate around the inflexible timing of farm responsibilities drives my staff crazy — but they know my farm work is non-negotiable. It keeps me, quite literally, grounded. **And rather than spend my days hobnobbing with Republican special interests, I rely on hard-working folks like you to power everything we do.** **[That’s why I’m personally asking you to join my reelection team and split $10 between Tammy Baldwin and my campaign today to help us block Mitch McConnell from taking back the Senate.
